subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for DataWave
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice@datwave.ai>, Bob Turner <bob@procurecorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for DataWave

Hi Alice & Bob,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the candid overview of DataWave's production requirements. Below is a short recap from our side to confirm the pain points, success criteria, and next steps so we can size Dedicated capacity appropriately. Please flag anything I missed or that needs adjustment.

Pain points / Drivers
- Unpredictable tail latency during nightly batch scoring and morning traffic spikes (latency SLO breaches ~5–10% at peak).
- Current infra is a mix of managed endpoints + ad-hoc on-prem GPUs; ops overhead and cold-start latency is impacting product SLAs.
- Need for clear isolation controls to meet procurement & security gating for customer data.

Current stack
- Model runtime: Triton-backed serving for some models; several large generative models (>30B) served via a custom FastAPI + GPU fleet.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes + custom autoscaler; SRE team handles model rollouts manually.
- Monitoring: Datadog + custom traces; no unified token-level cost breakdown today.

Success criteria for Dedicated fit
1) Predictable throughput: sustain 120–150 tokens/sec (aggregate) for the primary model under steady-state, with headroom for spikes to 300–400 TPS via burst capacity.
2) Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for interactive traffic during normal hours, and graceful degradation with fallbacks during spikes.
3) Isolation/data controls: physically reserved pool and network isolation to satisfy procurement + SOC2 evidence requests.
4) Ops: Automated canary rollouts and one-click rollback, with per-route dashboards for cost/latency.

Sizing / Autoscaling notes (high level)
- Based on the traffic profile you shared (avg queries: 18k/day, peak concurrency ~120 sessions/min), we think a 4–6 GPU reserved pool using A100-style instances with configured burst capacity should meet steady-state and allow headroom. Exact sizing depends on quantization and batching trades — Sean (cc'd) can run a quick perf run to finalize.
- Autoscaling policy: target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds + request queue length; burst capacity from shared reserved capacity for predictable spike coverage.

Next steps
1) Redwood: share preliminary Dedicated pricing and an example SLA + deployment topology (attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf).
2) DataWave: share 7-day load curve and any compliance docs needed for procurement (you mentioned procurement would want network diagrams & encryption at rest details).
3) Tech sync: Sean to run a quick perf test against a sample model (we'll coordinate time) and provide final sizing.
4) Procurement sync: Vanessa + Rachel to join a 30-min procurement call next week if helpful.

Attachments
- redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (preliminary pricing + SLA examples)

If that all looks right, I'll get Sean to schedule a perf run early next week and send an updated sizing + committed capacity recommendation.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Redwood Inference — making inference predictable and economical for engineering teams
From: Alice Chen <alice@datwave.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Dedicated capacity fit for DataWave

Thanks Vanessa — this matches our notes and is super helpful. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 120–150 tokens/sec figure is what our primary model averages during business hours; peak concurrency can push that to ~350 tokens/sec for short bursts (1–3 minutes) around morning digest generation.
- For the nightly batch scoring (runs ~2am PST), we need capacity to process a 12M-token job within a 3-hour window — we can share the job manifest.
- Procurement will want encryption at rest + key management info; happy to circulate a redline checklist if that helps.

I attached a 7-day load curve export (datawave-load-curve.csv) so you have the raw shape. Looking forward to Sean's perf run — can we aim for early next week (Mon/Tue)?

Best,
Alice
Head of Engineering, DataWave
alice@datwave.ai
